full_judgment: 3. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner, firstly, submits that the petition of complaint is not tenable in the eye of law as it was filed by the attorney of the Bank. He secondly, submits that the provision of section 247 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has direct application under the facts and circumstances of the present case in that on several dates the complainant-opposite party was found to be absent in the court for which the accused ought to have been acquitted. Thirdly, he submits that since a money suit for realisation of the said outstanding amount was filed by the opposite party No. 1 before filing of this complaint case and it has been decreed in favour of the complainant subsequent filing of the complainant case is an abuse of the process of law and court and liable to be quashed inasmuch as the complainant would get back his dues by executing the decree passed in his favour against the accused petitioner. But Mr Alam candidly concedes that the procedure in filing a case under section 138 of the Negotiable lnstruments Act in the present case have been duly complied with.
